en: Prosperity.
The Garland of Jewels of Questions and Answers
Who indeed would not be adorned by this "Jewel Garland of Questions and Answers," which, when worn around the neck, is so efficacious in accomplishing both seen and unseen goals? (1)
O Blessed One, what is to be accepted as the word of a guru, and what is to be rejected as that which should not be done?
Who is a guru—one who has realized the truth and is constantly intent on the welfare of his disciples? (2)
What must be done swiftly by the wise? The severing of the continuity of saṃsāra.
What is the seed of the tree of liberation? Right knowledge perfected through action. (3)
What is the most beneficial dharma? What is pure in this world—he whose mind is purified.
Who is wise? One who possesses discernment. What is poison? Disregard for one's gurus. (4)

Even when reflected upon repeatedly, what is the essence in cyclic existence? It is this alone: among human beings, that birth which is most cherished and dedicated to the welfare of oneself and others. (5)
What affection is like wine, producing delusion? What are the robbers? The objects of the senses. What is the creeper of worldly existence? Thirst. Who is the enemy? Lack of exertion. (6)
Why is there fear here of death? Who among those possessed by passion is superior here?
Who is a hero who has not been pierced by the arrows of a woman’s eyes? (7)
What nectar is fit here to be drunk with cupped palms? It is the instruction of the virtuous.
What is the root of greatness? It is this very thing called "freedom from begging. (8)
What is inscrutable? The conduct of women. Who is clever? He who has not been deceived by them. What is suffering? Dissatisfaction. What is meanness? Begging from the lowly. (9)

What is a life well-lived? That which is blameless. What is dullness? Non-practice even of what has been studied. Who is awake? The one possessed of discernment. What is sleep for a living being? Delusion. (10)
Is youth, wealth, and life as flickering as a drop of water upon a lotus leaf?
Tell me, moreover, who are equal to the rays of the moon? Only the virtuous. 11.

What is hell? Subjection to another's will. What is happiness? The renunciation of all attachments. What is truth? That which is beneficial to living beings and pleasing. And what is dear to living beings? Their very lives.
What is pride that yields no good result? What brings happiness? Friendship with the virtuous. Who is skillful in destroying all calamities? One who is entirely generous. 13.
What is death? Foolishness. And what is priceless? That which is given at the proper time. What is a thorn that lasts until death? A sin committed in secret. (14)
Where should effort be applied? In the study of knowledge, in wholesome medicine, and in giving charity.
Where should disregard be shown? Toward the wicked, the wives of others, and the wealth of others. 15.
What should be contemplated day and night? Not the worthlessness of women, but the worthlessness of saṃsāra.
What beloved should be practiced? Compassion toward the miserable and friendliness toward the virtuous. (16)
Whose self cannot be conquered even when the vital breaths have reached the throat—not the fool’s, nor the suspicious, nor the despondent, nor the ungrateful? 17.
Who is virtuous? One of good conduct. Whom do they call base? One of evil conduct. By what has this world been conquered? By the man who possesses truth and forbearance. (18)
To whom do the gods offer salutations? To him who is preeminent in compassion.
From what would fear of the forest of saṃsāra arise for the wise man? [From that same source. 19.
Under whose control does the multitude of living beings abide? Under that of one who speaks the truth and is disciplined.
Where should one stand? Upon the path of justice, for the sake of attaining both seen and unseen rewards.
Who is blind? He who is devoted to what ought not to be done. Who is deaf? He who does not listen to beneficial words.
Who is mute? He who does not know how to speak pleasant words at the proper time. (21)
What is the gift that is free from expectation? Who is the friend who restrains one from evil? What is the ornament? Virtuous conduct. And what is the adornment of speech? Truth. (22)
What is as fickle as the flash of lightning? The company of the wicked and young women.
Who remain unshakable in their lineage and character even in this Kali age? Only the virtuous.
What more can I say of that "Fourfold Auspiciousness" (caturbhadra), which is as difficult to find here as a wish-fulfilling gem?
Those who have shaken off all darkness speak of it specifically as such.
Generosity accompanied by kind speech, knowledge free from pride, valor endowed with patience, and wealth combined with renunciation—this fourfold excellence is difficult to find. (25)
What is to be lamented? Miserliness when one possesses wealth. What is praised? Generosity. Who is worthy of honor by the wise? He who is naturally humble at all times. (26)
Who is the sun for the lotus of his lineage—he who remains humble despite the abundance of his virtues?
Under whose sway is this world—of him who speaks words that are pleasing and beneficial, and who is devoted to the Dharma? (27)
What is that which captivates the minds of the wise? It is excellent poetry and the wife of one possessed of knowledge.
Whom does misfortune not touch—the self-controlled man who follows the words of those who have attained great advancement? 28.

For whom does Kamalā yearn? For one whose mind is unwearied and who conducts himself according to righteous policy. And whom does she suddenly abandon? One who reviles the twice-born, the preceptor, and the gods, as well as one who is indolent.
Where should one dwell? Either in the proximity of the virtuous or in Kāśī. Which region should be avoided? One that is filled with backbiters and ruled by a greedy king. (30)
By whom is a man not to be pitied—he who bows before his wife and possesses steady wealth?
And who in this world is to be pitied—he who, despite possessing wealth, is no giver? (31)
What is the root of baselessness among common men? It is begging.
And who is more brave than Rāma—he who, struck by the arrows of Love, does not waver? 32.
What should be contemplated day and night? Not saṃsāra, but the feet of the Blessed One. What men, though possessing eyes, would be blind? Those who are atheists.
Who here is renowned as a cripple? He who wanders to a sacred ford in his old age.
And what is the foremost of sacred fords? That which removes the impurity of the mind.

What should men always remember? The name of Hari. What language should not be spoken? The language of the Yavanas. What indeed should not be uttered by the wise? The faults of others, just as falsehood should not be spoken. 35.
What should be accomplished by men? Knowledge, wealth, strength, fame, and merit.
What is the destroyer of all virtues? Greed. And who is the enemy? Desire.
And which assembly should be avoided—that which is devoid of an aged counselor?
For where indeed in this world could a man find stability while serving a king? (37)
What is more delightful than one's own life? The family dharma and the company of the virtuous.
What must be guarded? One's reputation, devotion to one's husband, and one's own intellect. (38)
What in this world is the wish-fulfilling creeper? Knowledge imparted to a worthy disciple.
What would be the imperishable banyan tree? That gift which is bestowed according to the rules upon a deserving recipient. (39)

What is the weapon for all? [Discrimination]. What is the mother? [Skillful means]. And what is the cow? [The earth]. What indeed is strength? [Fortitude]. And what is death? [Lack of attentiveness]. (40)
Where is poison? Among wicked people. What here is impurity? Debt for those who owe it. What is fearlessness here? Detachment. And what is fear for everyone? Wealth alone. (41)
What is difficult for men to obtain? Devotion to Hari. And what indeed is sin? Violence.
Who would be dear to the Blessed One? He who, being himself undisturbed, does not disturb another. 42.
From what source does the success of austerity arise? Where indeed is wisdom found among the gods on earth (brāhmaṇas), and from where does that wisdom come?
It comes from serving the elders; who are the elders? Those who know the true essence of dharma.
What infamy could be greater than death for one who has been highly esteemed?
Who in this world can be truly happy, even if he possesses wealth; for what indeed is wealth other than that which is used for purposeful effort? 44.
What is the seed of all happiness? Merit. Whence does suffering arise? From sin. To whom belongs sovereignty? To him who indeed propitiates Śaṅkara with devotion. 45.
Who prospers? The humble one. Or who declines? The arrogant one.
Who is not to be trusted? He who speaks falsehood constantly. (46)
Wherein even a falsehood is sinless, as it has been said for the sake of protecting dharma? What is considered dharma by the cultured (śiṣṭas) who are well-born in their own lineage? 47.
What is the strength of the virtuous? What is destiny? Who is the virtuous person who is always contented?
What is destiny? It is merit (sukṛta). Who is the meritorious one? He who is praised by the wise. || 48 ||
And what is a friend for a householder? Who is his wife, and who is he that performs sacrifice?
What is sacrifice—that which is ordained by the Śruti and brings about the highest good for men? (49)

Whose action indeed is fruitful? That of one who is disciplined and possesses proper conduct. Who is disciplined? He who accepts the authority of the Vedas. And who is destroyed? He who has fallen away from ritual action. (50)
Who is the blessed renunciant? Who is the venerable scholar and saint?
Who is to be served? He who is a giver; and who is the giver? He who brings satisfaction to those who seek. || 51 ||
What is the fortune of embodied beings? Health. What kind of farmer reaps fruit?
He who sows. Of whom is there no sin? Of one who recites prayers. Who is truly fulfilled? He who possesses offspring.
What is difficult for men, if it is the constant restraint of the mind? Who would be a true practitioner of brahmacarya—he who is unswerving and whose vital seed is held aloft? (53)
And who is said to be the supreme deity? The power of consciousness (cicchakti). Who is the sustainer of the world? The sun. And what is the cause of life for all? That is Parjanya.

Who is the hero? He who is the protector of the frightened. And who is the protector? He is the Guru. For who indeed is called the Teacher of the World? Śambhu. From whom does knowledge come? From Śiva alone. 55.
From what can one obtain liberation? From devotion to Mukunda. Who is Mukunda?
He who delivers one from ignorance. What is ignorance? It is the non-manifestation of the Self. 56.
For whom is there no sorrow? For one who is free from anger. What is happiness? Contentment. Who is a king? One who acts with kindness. And who is a dog? He who serves the base. (57)
Who is the supreme Lord who is a magician? What is this phenomenal world that acts like a magical illusion?
What is this waking experience that resembles a dream? And what is the reality, even though it is Brahman? 58.
What is false? That which is to be destroyed by knowledge, such as the void thing of a hare's horn and the like.
And what is the indeterminable illusion (māyā)? What is the imagined duality? 59.
What would be the ultimate reality? How could non-duality and ignorance be beginningless? What nourishes the body, what is the prārabdha, and what is life-giving food? (60)
Who is that Śambhu who is to be worshipped by the Brāhmaṇas, whose sphere is the Gāyatrī, the Sun, and Fire?
And what indeed is that ultimate reality within the Gāyatrī, the Sun, the Fire, and Śambhu? 61.
Who is the mother who is a manifest deity? Who, O father, is the venerable guru?
Who is the Brahmin who embodies all deities and is endowed with learning and ritual action? 62.
And what was the cause of the destruction of the lineage, and what was the distress inflicted upon the virtuous?
Whose words are unfailing, and who are those whose nature is truth, silence, and tranquility? (63)
What is birth? Attachment to sense objects. What is the subsequent birth? It would be a son. Who is unavoidable? Death. And where should one place one's step? In that which is purified by vision. 64.
Who is the worthy recipient for the gift of food? Who is truly hungry? Indeed, who is the incarnation of the Blessed One?
And who is the Blessed One? It is Maheśa, the singular self of Śaṅkara and Nārāyaṇa. (65)
What is the fruit of devotion to the Blessed One? It is the direct perception of the nature of that world.
And what is liberation? It is the cessation of ignorance. What is the source of all the Vedas? It is Om. (66)
Thus, those who have this "Jewel Garland of Questions and Answers" fixed upon their throats shine in the assemblies of the virtuous, stainless as if adorned with pearls. (67)

Thus ends the *Praśnottararatnamālikā*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (*paramahaṃsaparivrājakācārya*).
